staffIdentityAndDirectory: src/staff-identity.mjs (all three repos, byte-identical) -- provider-agnostic OIDC/JWKS verifier, RS256-only, fail-closed on every branch, returns null for a non-JWT bearer (fall-through signal), a typed refusal for a JWT-shaped-but-invalid bearer (terminal), or {ok:true, identity} on success. Does not itself enforce any maximum token age beyond exp/nbf -- the gap G-134 GAP 3 exists to close.

src/staff-directory.mjs (smartcity-dashboards only) -- upsertStaffAccount/disableStaffAccount/isStaffAccountRevoked, Neon-backed with an in-memory fallback when DATABASE_URL is unset. Explicitly documents itself as 'not the provisioning mechanism' and names staff-admin-client.mjs as the file that plugs into it -- this is the seam GAP 1 fills.

src/tenancy.mjs resolveCaller -- staff bearer checked first via the Authorization header only, prior to this lane; no cookie fallback existed, meaning a browser sign-in flow (which sets a cookie, not a header) had nowhere to deliver its credential. This is the reason GAP 5 required a tenancy.mjs change, not only new routes.
planReviewIntegrationPattern: src/actors.mjs staffEngagementRefusal + src/server.mjs resolveStaffCaller (plan-review) -- the dispatch names this the pattern to mirror for GAP 4. Read in full before writing smart-files' equivalent.
smartFilesReadPath: src/server.mjs requireReadScope / bearerToken / resolveCallerIdentity (identity.mjs) -- smart-files' existing read-scope gate resolves an OPAQUE SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKENS bearer from the SAME Authorization header slot a staff JWT would arrive in. This is the actual integration point (not an 'x-persona header' as the dispatch's prose suggested -- smart-files uses body-based orgId/userId for QA personas, not a header; the read path's caller identity is a completely separate, service-token-based mechanism). verifyStaffToken's null-for-non-JWT contract is what lets a staff JWT and an opaque service token share one header slot safely.

operatorDirectionMidSession: Asked the user directly how to proceed given the missing WorkOS account (three options: build-now-verify-later, wait for a real key, or stop and report blocked). Answer: build now, verify later -- build GAP 1/4/5 against WorkOS's documented API with full unit-test coverage against mocked responses, and state plainly in the close that live account-creation/sign-in was not verified against a real organization.
